leftEvidence.title: Joshua and Caleb call the land exceedingly good

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses and Aaron fall before the assembly; Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and call the land exceedingly good.
points.right: Caleb recalls being forty when Moses sent him from Kadesh Barnea and bringing back an honest report while others made the people afraid.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: They say the LORD will bring Israel in if he delights in them, forbid rebellion and fear, and are threatened with stoning before the LORD’s glory appears.
points.right: At eighty-five he asks for the hill country, still names Anakim and fortified cities, and trusts that the LORD may drive them out.

payload.posture: Caleb’s later appeal remembers the same danger and his full following decades after he urged Israel to enter.

rightEvidence.role: Another spying mission and the delayed inheritance
rightEvidence.title: Caleb receives the land he followed the LORD to seek

payload.tension: The inheritance fulfills the earlier exception while retaining Anakim, fortified cities, and dependence on the LORD.
payload.title: Caleb’s report and his inheritance
